{{nihongo|'''Tsuno Shrine'''|都農神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Hyūga Province]].

``Tsuno Shrine'' is located in {{ill|Miyazaki Prefecture|Q130300|qid=Q130300}}{{ill|Koyu District, Miyazaki|Q1132169|qid=Q1132169}}{{ill|Tsuno, Miyazaki|Q1205974|qid=Q1205974}}. {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}, {{ill|Hyūga Province|Q513737|qid=Q513737}}{{ill|Ichinomiya|Q1656379|qid=Q1656379}}. {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Old Shrine Ranking}} is {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Old Shrine}} is {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Kokuhei-kosha}}, and currently it is {{ill|Beppyo shrine|Q10898274|qid=Q10898274}} of {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|Q908077|qid=Q908077}}.

Before {{ill|Meiji era|ar|فترة مييجي|ast|Dómina Meiji|az|Meydzi dövrü|azb|مئی‌جی دؤورو|be|Перыяд Мэйдзі|bn|মেইজি যুগ|bo|མེའི་ཇིའི་དུས་དུས་མཚམས།|ca|Era Meiji|cs|Období Meidži|da|Meiji-perioden|de|Meiji-Zeit|el|Μεϊτζί (περίοδος)|es|Era Meiji|et|Meiji periood|eu|Meiji Aroa|fa|دوره میجی|fi|Meiji-kausi|fr|Ère Meiji|gl|Período Meiji|he|תקופת מייג'י|hr|Meiji (razdoblje)|ht|Epòk Meiji|hu|Meidzsi-kor|id|Zaman Meiji|io|Ero Meiji|is|Meiji-tímabilið|it|Periodo Meiji|ja|明治|ka|მეიძის ეპოქა|kbp|Mejii wɛɛ yaa alɩwaatʊ|kk|Мэйдзи дәуірі|ko|메이지 시대|la|Aetas Meiji|lt|Meidži laikotarpis|lv|Meidzi periods|mk|Меиџи (период)|mn|Мэйжийн эрин|ms|Zaman Meiji|nl|Meijiperiode|nn|Meiji|no|Meiji-perioden|pl|Meiji (okres)|pt|Era Meiji|ro|Perioada Meiji|ru|Мэйдзи|simple|Meiji period|sk|Obdobie Meidži|sq|Periudha Meixhi|sr|Меиџи период|sv|Meijiperioden|ta|மெய்சி காலம்|th|ยุคเมจิ|tl|Panahong Meiji|tr|Meiji Dönemi|uk|Період Мейдзі|ur|میجی دور|vi|Thời kỳ Minh Trị|war|Panahon Meiji|wuu|明治|zh|明治|zh_classical|明治|zh_min_nan|Bêng-tī|zh_yue|明治|qid=Q3125096}}, it was also called ``Miyazaki-sha'' and ``Miyazaki-miya''. It is also called ``Ichinomiya Shrine'' locally.

=== Enshrined God ===
* '''{{ill|Ōkuninushi|Q276944|qid=Q276944|lt=Ōmi Takamikoto}}''' (Onamuchi Mikoto)
*: Same as Okuninushi no Mikoto. Since it has been the guardian deity of the Tsuno-cho area since ancient times, it is said that it was dedicated to the deity of the land.

Furthermore, ``{{ill|Chiribukuro|Q17213633|qid=Q17213633}}'' has the text ``Tsu no Daimyojin.''<ref>There is a theory that this article in ``Kinbukuro'' is an anecdote from ``{{ill|Fudoki|Q1194534|qid=Q1194534|lt=Hyuga Province Fudoki}},'' but this is being questioned (Iwanami Japanese Classical Literature Compendium ``Fudōki''). </ref>, ``{{ill|Jinten Ainōshō|Q30928164|qid=Q30928164}}'' adds an additional note to it and states that it is a miraculous cure for {{ill|Smallpox|Q12214|qid=Q12214|lt=smallpox}}. It was also believed that it would remove insect damage from the fields.

=== History ===

=== Founding ===
According to the shrine's legend, {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|Q200188|qid=Q200188}} began worshiping the shrine six years before his ascension to the throne, when the Emperor was en route to the {{ill|Jimmu's Eastern Expedition|Q11590444|qid=Q11590444|lt=Eastern Conquest}}. </ref>. In addition, an article in ``Jinzoe Ibukuro'' that says that {{ill|Empress Jingū|Q232803|qid=Q232803}} solicited ``Tuno Daimyojin'' as a guardian deity for boats during the {{ill|Three Han Campaign|ja|三韓征伐|ko|삼한 정벌|zh|三韩征伐|qid=Q11249435}} <ref>This article is already in ``Jinbukuro'' and, as mentioned in the previous note, is regarded as an anecdote from ``Fudoki''. Citing </ref>, it is reported that the shrine was first built by the Empress after her triumphant return. Similarly, in ``{{ill|Chiribukuro|Q17213633|qid=Q17213633}}'', when Empress Jingu returned from the Sanhan Conquest, when she shot a bow at ``Bama-no-mine'', a black head appeared out of the soil, so she dug it up in the mountain, and two people, a man and a woman, appeared, and she summoned them as {{ill|Jinin|Q11588676|qid=Q11588676}}.

In addition to ruins dating back to the {{ill|Jōmon period|Q52824|qid=Q52824}}, there are more than 20 ancient tombs (Tsuno kofun group) such as {{ill|Round Kofun|Q11394747|qid=Q11394747}} and {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|Q11268718|qid=Q11268718}}, and pottery and stone tools have been excavated near our company's shrine. It is known that people lived there from an early time, and the history of our company as a guardian deity dates back to ancient times.

=== Outline ===
{{ill|Jōwa (Heian period)|Q1075605|qid=Q1075605|lt=Jowa}} In the 4th year ({{ill|837|Q25093|qid=Q25093}}), he was promoted to a government shrine, and in the 10th year of Jowa ({{ill|843|Q23469|qid=Q23469}}), he was given the rank of Junior Fifth Rank (hereinafter referred to as ``{{ill|Shoku Nihon Kōki|Q1041301|qid=Q1041301}}''), {{ill|Ten'an|Q1075611|qid=Q1075611|lt=Ten'an}} In 2nd year ({{ill|858|Q30371|qid=Q30371}}), he was promoted to Jushii (Junior Fourth Rank) ("{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Q1052981|qid=Q1052981}}"). In "{{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}" {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932|lt=Shinmyocho}}, ``'''Tsuno Shrine'''' is written in {{ill|Hyūga Province|Q513737|qid=Q513737}}{{ill|Koyu District, Miyazaki|Q1132169|qid=Q1132169}}, and it is listed as {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shinouchi Shrine}}. It is said that at that time it was the largest shrine in Hyuga Province, with a magnificent shrine building and vast grounds. It is said that this position caused a political and religious conflict with {{ill|Tsuma Shrine|Q3541658|qid=Q3541658}}, which is listed in <ref name="Gods">Tsunō Shrine in ``Japanese Gods''. </ref>As will be explained later, the details are not clear because the ancient documents were destroyed.It is certain that our company was revered not only by the common people but also by the local feudal lords as ``Ichinomiya of Hyuga Province'', and in {{ill|Tenbun|Q1192853|qid=Q1192853|lt=Tenbun}}18 ({{ill|1549|Q6554|qid=Q6554}}), the shrine building was rebuilt by {{ill|Itō Yoshisuke|Q6095349|qid=Q6095349}}. Later, in {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Q1145058|qid=Q1145058}}6 ({{ill|1578|Q6707|qid=Q6707}}), during the conflict between the Otomo and Shimazu armies, {{ill|Ōtomo Sōrin|Q1185032|qid=Q1185032|lt=Otomo Sorin}} and {{ill|Shimazu Yoshihisa|es|Shimazu Yoshihisa|fa|شیمازو یوشی‌هیسا|fr|Shimazu Yoshihisa|it|Shimazu Yoshihisa|ja|島津義久|ko|시마즈 요시히사 (1533년)|mr|शिमाझु योशिहिसा|ru|Симадзу Ёсихиса|zh|島津義久|qid=Q955727}}. Anniversary of Emperor Jimmu's Transfer to the East.'' After the war, it belonged to {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|Q908077|qid=Q908077}}, and in 1948 ({{ill|1948|Q5165|qid=Q5165}}) It became Omote Shrine|Q10898274}}, and the main shrine was rebuilt in {{ill|Heisei era|Q234510|qid=Q234510}}19 ({{ill|2007|Q2024|qid=Q2024}}).

=== God level ===
* In August of {{ill|Jōwa (Heian period)|Q1075605|qid=Q1075605|lt=Jowa}} 4th year ({{ill|837|Q25093|qid=Q25093}}), it was promoted to a government shrine (``{{ill|Shoku Nihon Kōki|Q1041301|qid=Q1041301}}'') - It is written as ``Shitonojin.''
*September 19, 10th year of Jowa ({{ill|843|Q23469|qid=Q23469}}), from no rank to junior fifth rank ("Shoku Nihon Koki") - Written as "Tsuno Kojin".
* {{ill|Ten'an|Q1075611|qid=Q1075611|lt=Ten'an}} October 22, 2nd year ({{ill|858|Q30371|qid=Q30371}}), from the upper fifth rank to the upper fourth rank (``{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Q1052981|qid=Q1052981}}'')

=== Precincts ===
[[File:Tsuno-jinja honden.JPG|thumb|200px|right|main hall]]
The main shrine is {{ill|Nagare-zukuri|Q210684|qid=Q210684|lt=Ikkensha Nagaruzou}} with a copper plate roof and {{ill|chigi and katsuogi|Q87220234|qid=Q87220234}}. It was rebuilt in 2007 and largely follows the shape of the old main shrine. The old main shrine was rebuilt in 1986 with a donation from Kinosuke Kono, and it has now been relocated and serves as the main shrine of Kumano Shrine, a subsidiary shrine.

The worship hall, like the main shrine, was rebuilt in 2007. It is a {{ill|East Asian hip-and-gable roof|Q855025|qid=Q855025}} with 5 rooms in the front and 3 spaces on the sides, and a {{ill|Kirizuma-style|Q13308575|qid=Q13308575}} tsumairi shrine with a depth of 2 ken in the center of the back. The roof is made of copper sheets, with a {{ill|Bargeboard|Q4881511|qid=Q4881511|lt=staggered gable}} on the front, and below that is a three-room {{ill|kōhai|Q11415970|qid=Q11415970}} with a gable and a gable in the center. The old worship hall has been relocated and is now used as a kagura hall.

In ancient times, the Ichi-no-Torii gate was located near Tsuno High School ({{Coord|32|15|06.90|N|131|33|43.93|E|region:JP-45_type:landmark|name=Ichi-no-Torii ruins}}), and its size shows the power of the past.

=== Okumiya ===

* '''Taki Shrine''
** Enshrined deity: {{ill|Kuraokami|Q644201|qid=Q644201|lt=Takani no Mikoto}}
*: It is located approximately 1km northeast of our company ({{Coord|32|16|21.07|N|131|33|04.20|E|region:JP-45_type:landmark|name=Okumiya: Taki Shrine}}). It enshrines the ``Fudo-no-taki'' waterfall that flows behind the shrine.

=== Main festivals ===
* Summer Festival ({{ill|August 1|Q2788|qid=Q2788}}-{{ill|August 2|Q2785|qid=Q2785|lt=2nd}})
*: Also called the ``Goshinko Festival,'' {{ill|Mikoshi|Q979940|qid=Q979940}} is paraded around Tsuno Town. It is said that the name comes from the fact that Empress Jingu brought the enshrined deity of the company to her boat as a guardian deity during the Sanhan Conquest, and there was a time when it was discontinued, but it was revived in {{ill|Tenpō|Q1369045|qid=Q1369045}}3 ({{ill|1832|Q7584|qid=Q7584}}).
* Winter Festival ({{ill|December 4|Q2310|qid=Q2310}}-{{ill|December 5|Q2300|qid=Q2300|lt=5th}})
*: Kagura is played throughout the night, and the annual festival is held on the 5th. Also, on that day, it is said that if a woman suffering from breast ailments offers a ladle, she will be cured.
